answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token stake before it can trade, then build reputation through signed transactions with long lived counterparties. A committee chosen by verifiable randomness periodically audits identity links and slashes stake when aliases collude or recycle funds. Creating many fake agents therefore multiplies capital locked and exposes more connections to detection; splitting one stake across aliases also lowers each account’s trading limit. The lotus registry preserves a relic record, while an ember account remains untrusted.
